Priya S.: Hey team, customer (Ledgerly) hit a production outage — structured JSON responses intermittently invalid when the model returns file paths. They see unparseable payloads from our /v1/generate structured output mode. Example response fragment they get: 

Priya S.: ```json
{
  "transaction_id": "tx_9f7",
  "note": "Saved to C:\\invoices\\"
}
```

Priya S.: Parsers choke because the string ends with a single backslash before the closing quote (looks like "\" in the stream). This only happens sporadically. Customer reports it correlates with high QPS and when they use prefix caching on our SDK.

Alex M.: Can you paste the request they used? also, which model + runtime?

Priya S.: cURL repro they gave (redacted api key):

Priya S.: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-orca-v1","mode":"structured","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"transaction_id":{"type":"string"},"note":{"type":"string"}}},"prompt":"Return JSON with file path note. Example: \"Saved to C:\\\\invoices\\\\\"","enable_kv_cache":true}'
```

Priya S.: Repro notes: when enable_kv_cache=true we sometimes see the broken string. When enable_kv_cache=false the response is consistently valid (double-escaped backslashes like C:\\invoices).

eng-ml-bot: Auto-detected runtime: serving-pool-03 (cuda-rt 2.6). Tokenizer boundary observed at token idx 134 in failing traces. Suspected issue: prefix/KV stitching leaves an unescaped backslash at chunk end which next chunk doesn't re-escape, producing an unterminated escape sequence in JSON.

Alex M.: OK that points at KV cache prefix stitching. Priya, can you confirm a minimal repro where prompt ends with a backslash in the cached prefix (e.g., prompt = "root dir: C:\\myapp\\" and then generation continues)? If you can confirm, please collect the raw token stream and the runtime trace (we need the token ids around the boundary).

Priya S.: Confirmed quick test: make cached prefix = "Path: C:\\temp\\" then short generation for note. With kv cache ON we get invalid JSON. With kv cache OFF we get valid JSON. Attaching small trace snippet from customer logs: 

Priya S.: ```
[serving-pool-03] prefix_tokens: [..., 981, 45, 12]  # 12 corresponds to trailing backslash token
[serving-pool-03] cached_kv_chunk: length=8
[serving-pool-03] emit_chunk: tokens start with 34 (quote) but runtime produced sequence: 92 34  --> "\\\"\"
[serving-pool-03] reconstructed bytes: ... C:\\invoices\"  <-- missing escape for trailing backslash
```

Sana K.: This looks like a classical boundary-escape stitch bug. Could be tokenizer-dependent (some tokenizers emit a single backslash token). Workarounds: 1) client-side: escape backslashes in inputs (replace "\\" with "\\\\"). 2) API: temporarily disable KV cache for the customer's route. 3) Server: sanitize outputs by canonicalizing escapes before streaming.

Alex M.: Can we reproduce in-house on serving-pool-03? I'll spin a quick test harness that toggles enable_kv_cache and dumps token ids. If reproducible we should escalate to eng-runtime with P1 since it's corrupting customer data.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1145 (priority P1) — assigned to eng-runtime.

Priya S.: Customer on an elevated support plan; they want a fix or a recommended mitigation ASAP. I've suggested disabling kv cache for their tenant and to escape backslashes in the short term.

eng-ml-bot: Notes to runtime team: look at prefix re-encoding path in kv-stitcher. Pay special attention to tokens that represent backslash (92) and how we merge the last token of cached prefix with first token of generation. Also check any fast-path that assumes "no escaping needed" when concatenating cached strings.

Sana K.: I'll draft an internal repro and add it to the INC ticket with exact cURL + expected vs observed bytes. If anyone has a quick patch suggestion for a safe server-side mitigation (pre-stream sanitization to enforce valid JSON escapes), post here.

Alex M.: I'll attach my local test output to the ticket in ~45m. Thanks. :thumbsup:
